title: It Was a Record-Breaking Year for Dust Storms
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentIt Was a Record-Breaking Year for Dust StormsThe worst since the Dust Bowl in some placesDNBy David Nield11:00 AM CDT on July 21, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleEvery year the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) puts out a Dust Bulletin—a record of how many sand and dust storms hit our planet over a 12-month period which notes how dangerous those storms might be for air quality, health, and the environment.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 103.4K 00OTD In Space - November 25: 1st Powered Flight of the 'Wingless' M2-F3 AircraftShareNextStayThe July 2026 bulletin has now arrived, covering the year 2025, and while the overall dust surface concentrations were comparable to 2024, there were certain areas that were significantly impacted by dust and sand storms—to a record-breaking level, in some cases.STORMY SKIES: Dust storms across Oklahoma and Texas, March 14, 2025.
